question: What is the taboo name (birth name) of Kinh Duong Vuong and whose son is he?
answer: The taboo name (birth name) of Kinh Duong Vuong is **Kinh Duong**, and he is the son of **Hung Vuong**.

question: When they separated, how did Lac Long Quan and Au Co divide their children?
answer:
In Vietnamese mythology, Lac Long Quan and Au Co had a total of 100 children. When they decided to separate, they divided their children as follows:

- Lac Long Quan took the **first 50 children**, who were born with **long hair**.
- Au Co took the **remaining 50 children**, who were born with **short hair**.

This division is a significant part of the legend, symbolizing the separation of the two deities and the beginning of the Vietnamese people's origin story.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. question: What were the officials in charge of affairs under Hung Vuong called and what were their hereditary characteristics?
answer: Under Hung Vuong, the officials in charge of affairs were called **Bo Chinh**. Their hereditary characteristic was that they passed down their positions from father to son, a system referred to as **phu dao**.

{"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

The king was a man of sagacious intelligence; De Minh loved him dearly and wanted him to succeed to the throne. The king persistently yielded to his older brother and dared not obey the command. De Minh then established De Nghi as the heir to rule the North, and enfeoffed the king as Kinh Duong Vuong to rule the South, calling it the kingdom of Xich Quy.
The king married the daughter of Dong Dinh Quan named Than Long, and fathered Lac Long Quan (Note: The Tang annals record: during the Kinh Duong period, there was a goat-herding woman who claimed to be the youngest daughter of Dong Dinh Quan; she married the second son of Kinh Xuyen but was abandoned, and wrote a letter asking Lieu Nghi to report this to Dong Dinh Quan. One day, the king said to Au Co: "I am of the dragon race, you are of the fairy race; water and fire are incompatible, it is truly difficult for us to be together." They then bid each other farewell, dividing 50 children to follow their mother to the mountains, and 50 children to follow their father to the South (some versions record to the South Sea), and enfeoffed the eldest son as Hung Vuong to succeed the throne.

It was this teacher who discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel to build a great enterprise. question: When Thuy Tinh raised the waters to attack Tan Vien, what methods did Son Tinh use to fight back?
answer: In the legend of Son Tinh and Thuy Tinh, when Thuy Tinh raised the waters to attack Tan Vien, Son Tinh fought back by calling upon the mountains to rise and block the flood. This act of defiance symbolized the struggle between the forces of earth and water, with Son Tinh representing the mountainous terrain and Thuy Tinh representing the flowing waters. The story highlights the natural elements' conflict and the balance of power between them.

question: Who later inherited Thuc Vuong's resentment and conquered Van Lang?
answer:
The answer is **Thuc Phan**. 

According to the legend, **Thuc Vuong** (the father of Thuc Phan) harbored resentment after being rejected by the king of Van Lang when he sought to marry the king's daughter, Mi Nuong. This resentment led him to instruct his descendants to destroy Van Lang and seize the country. It was **Thuc Phan**, one of his descendants, who possessed both courage and strategy, and he ultimately attacked and conquered Van Lang.

{"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

{"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

question: Who were the three brothers of the Tay Son movement?
answer:
The three brothers of the Tay Son movement were known as the **Tay Son tam kiệt** (Three Heroes of the Tay Son). They were:

1. **Nguyen Nhac** (Emperor Thai Duc) – The eldest brother, who was the first emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty.
2. **Nguyen Hue** (Quang Trung) – The second brother, who became the second emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his brother Nguyen Nhac abdicated.
3. **Nguyen Lu** (Quang Toan) – The youngest brother, who succeeded Nguyen Hue as the third emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty but was very young when he took the throne.

Together, they led the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war and unified Vietnam under their rule.

question: At what age did Quang Trung die, and what happened to the Tay Son Dynasty after his death?
answer:
Quang Trung, also known as Nguyen Hue, died at the age of 34. He passed away on December 18, 1792, following a brief illness.

After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty faced significant challenges. His brother, Nguyen Lu, succeeded him as the leader of the dynasty. However, Nguyen Lu was less capable and ambitious compared to Quang Trung. The dynasty began to decline due to internal strife, weak leadership, and external pressures from the northern Nguyen Lords and the French colonizers.

Eventually, the Tay Son Dynasty fell in 1802 when Nguyen Anh, the son of the Nguyen Lord of the North, defeated both Nguyen Lu and the remaining Tay Son forces. Nguyen Anh then established the Nguyen Dynasty, which ruled Vietnam until the 20th century.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. {"reference_id": "", "content": ""Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery (2010). Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production

Rihanna's approval of the song's topic ultimately influenced her decision to work with Eminem.
The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

question: Summarize the main reforms of Quang Trung during his reign.
answer:
During his reign, Quang Trung (Nguyen Hue) implemented several significant reforms that strengthened the Tay Son dynasty and improved governance across Vietnam. The main reforms included:

1. **Administrative Reforms**: Quang Trung reorganized the administrative structure of the country, centralizing power and improving efficiency. He established a more effective bureaucracy to manage the vast territories under his control.

2. **Military Reforms**: He reformed the military to make it more disciplined and effective. He emphasized the importance of martial arts and physical training, which contributed to the strength of the Tay Son forces. He also promoted the development of various martial arts styles, which played a crucial role in military training and combat.

3. **Economic Reforms**: Quang Trung focused on economic recovery and development. He encouraged agricultural production and trade, which helped stabilize the economy and improve the livelihoods of the people.

4. **Legal and Social Reforms**: He introduced legal reforms to ensure justice and fairness, and he promoted social harmony by reducing corruption and improving the treatment of the common people.

5. **Cultural and Educational Reforms**: Quang Trung supported cultural and educational initiatives, which helped in the intellectual and moral development of the populace. He also emphasized the importance of education in fostering a sense of national identity and unity.

These reforms collectively contributed to the stability, prosperity, and strength of the Tay Son dynasty during Quang Trung's reign.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. It became one of the most successful songs of the year, reaching number one on the Billboard Hot 100 chart.

{"reference_id": "", "content": ""Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery (2010). Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production

Rihanna's approval of the song's topic ultimately influenced her decision to work with Eminem.
The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

Recording
Mike Strange recorded and mixed Eminem's vocals at Effigy Studios in Ferndale, Michigan.[19] The sessions took two days.[20] Strange edited the vocals with D-Verb—a reverberation software—and an Extra Long Delay plug-in. He preferred to make few changes; for "Love the Way You Lie" he almost exclusively used board compression and console equalization. Strange used the Bricasti and Eventide Reverb 2016 mixing tools for "brighter" reverberation. Detroit musician Luis Resto has contributed to the arrangement on many of Eminem's songs, but did not do so for "Love the Way You Lie". According to Strange, "Everything we needed was already in the track, apart from the vocals."[2] Two to three weeks after the sessions, Alex da Kid arrived to help mix and master the track.[11] He wanted to replace the acoustic guitar on the demo, but Eminem chose to keep it.[3] Strange said, "It was simply a matter of trying to match and then to improve on the demo [Alex da Kid]'d sent us."[2] Strange's brother Joe engineered the track.[19]

Rihanna's recording sessions took place at Sun Studios in Dublin, Ireland, and were engineered by Marcos Tovar. The R&B songwriter Makeba Riddick provided additional vocal production.[19] Strange used equalization, compression and reverberation but left the vocal balance. He assumed that Rihanna was satisfied with her recorded vocals and did not make major changes on her seven stereo vocal tracks.[2]

Release and response
On May 27, 2010, Eminem revealed the title of "Love the Way You Lie" as part of the track list of his seventh studio album Recovery,[35] which came out on June 21.[36] Initially a radio single,[37] the song was released later by Polydor Records as a CD in the United Kingdom on August 9, 2010.[1] Interscope Records distributed it in Germany on August 20.[38]

"Love the Way You Lie" received generally favorable reviews. An editor for Rap-Up listed it among the four best tracks from the album.[39] New York Times writer Jon Caramanica considered it "one of the album's most engaging songs" and praised Eminem's ability to assess issues from the perspectives of both sexes.[40] MTV's Rodriguez wrote that the song echoes content from Eminem's earlier albums, but finds him "sober" and "more mature".[41] He added that the lyrics allude to Eminem's relationship with Scott and that "Love the Way You Lie" is his closest approach to a love song.[30] Editors of The A.V. {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Origins and Education

Origins of the Tay Son lineage

According to the books Khâm định Việt sử Thông giám cương mục and Đại Nam thực lục: Nguyen Hue's ancestors were from Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An region. Around the Thinh Duc years (reign name of Le Than Tong) (1653–1657), they were captured by Lord Nguyen's army and brought back to live in Tuy Vien district, Hoai Nhon prefecture. Several generations later, Nguyen Nhac held the position of a minor clerk (Biện lại) at the Van Don tollgate. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

"Love the Way You Lie" is a hip-hop song, specifically a rap song, and it is part of the hip-hop subgenre known as "trap" or "modern hip-hop." The song is a collaboration between Eminem and Rihanna, and it features a blend of hip-hop, pop, and electronic elements.

In Eminem's rap sections, the following instruments and elements are typically used:

1. **Drum Machine**: A prominent electronic drum pattern that provides the beat and rhythm.
2. **Synth Bass**: A deep, pulsing bassline that adds a rhythmic and melodic foundation.
3. **Synth Leads**: High-pitched, melodic synth lines that often complement the rap sections.
4. **Kick Drum**: A strong, deep kick drum that drives the beat.
5. **Hi-Hats**: Quick, snappy hi-hats that add texture and rhythm to the track.
6. **Electronic Effects**: Various electronic effects such as reverb, delay, and distortion are used to enhance the sound and create a more dynamic atmosphere.

These elements combine to create the signature sound of "Love the Way You Lie," which is characterized by its intense, aggressive energy and emotional depth.

{"reference_id": "", "content": ""Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery (2010). Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production

The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

Rihanna's recording sessions took place at Sun Studios in Dublin, Ireland, and were engineered by Marcos Tovar. {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Origins and Education

Origins of the Tay Son lineage

He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Origins and Education

Origins of the Tay Son lineage

According to the books Khâm định Việt sử Thông giám cương mục and Đại Nam thực lục: Nguyen Hue's ancestors were from Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An region. {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. question: Why did the music video for "Love the Way You Lie" receive mixed reactions?
answer:
The music video for "Love the Way You Lie" by Rihanna and Eminem received mixed reactions for several reasons, primarily due to its portrayal of domestic violence and the complex emotions it evoked in viewers. Here's a breakdown of the key factors contributing to the mixed responses:

1. **Portrayal of Domestic Violence**: The video depicts a tumultuous and abusive relationship, with scenes of physical and emotional abuse. While some viewers found the portrayal realistic and relatable, others found it disturbing and potentially harmful, especially for those who have experienced or are currently in abusive relationships.

2. **Emotional Complexity**: The song and video explore themes of love, regret, and the cyclical nature of abuse. This emotional complexity resonated with many, as it reflects the real-life struggles of individuals in toxic relationships. However, it also sparked debates about the responsibility of artists in depicting such sensitive and potentially triggering content.

3. **Artistic Expression vs. Real-Life Impact**: Some critics and fans argued that the video was a form of artistic expression that highlighted the complexities of human relationships. Others, however, felt that it could glamorize or normalize domestic violence, which raised ethical concerns about the role of media in shaping public perception.

4. **Cultural and Social Context**: The video was released in a cultural context where discussions about domestic violence and gender dynamics were gaining more attention. This context influenced how the video was received, with some viewing it as a powerful commentary on these issues and others as a potentially harmful depiction.

5. **Mixed Public Reaction**: The mixed reactions reflect the diverse perspectives on the portrayal of domestic violence in media. While some praised the video for its honesty and emotional depth, others criticized it for potentially contributing to the normalization of abusive behavior.

In summary, the mixed reactions to the "Love the Way You Lie" music video stem from its portrayal of domestic violence, the emotional complexity it presents, and the broader cultural and social context in which it was received. These factors led to a range of opinions, from appreciation for its artistic and emotional depth to concerns about its potential impact on viewers.

The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production
Rihanna with red, long hair and a dress with floral patterns. Her left hand is raised and her right-hand holds a microphone near her mouth.
Rihanna's approval of the song's topic ultimately influenced her decision to work with Eminem.
The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

Recording
Mike Strange recorded and mixed Eminem's vocals at Effigy Studios in Ferndale, Michigan.[19] The sessions took two days.[20] Strange edited the vocals with D-Verb—a reverberation software—and an Extra Long Delay plug-in. He preferred to make few changes; for "Love the Way You Lie" he almost exclusively used board compression and console equalization. Strange used the Bricasti and Eventide Reverb 2016 mixing tools for "brighter" reverberation. Detroit musician Luis Resto has contributed to the arrangement on many of Eminem's songs, but did not do so for "Love the Way You Lie". According to Strange, "Everything we needed was already in the track, apart from the vocals."[2] Two to three weeks after the sessions, Alex da Kid arrived to help mix and master the track.[11] He wanted to replace the acoustic guitar on the demo, but Eminem chose to keep it.[3] Strange said, "It was simply a matter of trying to match and then to improve on the demo [Alex da Kid]'d sent us."[2] Strange's brother Joe engineered the track.[19]

Rihanna's recording sessions took place at Sun Studios in Dublin, Ireland, and were engineered by Marcos Tovar. The R&B songwriter Makeba Riddick provided additional vocal production.[19] Strange used equalization, compression and reverberation but left the vocal balance. He assumed that Rihanna was satisfied with her recorded vocals and did not make major changes on her seven stereo vocal tracks.[2]

Release and response
On May 27, 2010, Eminem revealed the title of "Love the Way You Lie" as part of the track list of his seventh studio album Recovery,[35] which came out on June 21.[36] Initially a radio single,[37] the song was released later by Polydor Records as a CD in the United Kingdom on August 9, 2010.[1] Interscope Records distributed it in Germany on August 20.[38]

"Love the Way You Lie" received generally favorable reviews. {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Origins and Education

Origins of the Tay Son lineage

According to the books Khâm định Việt sử Thông giám cương mục and Đại Nam thực lục: Nguyen Hue's ancestors were from Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An region. Around the Thinh Duc years (reign name of Le Than Tong) (1653–1657), they were captured by Lord Nguyen's army and brought back to live in Tuy Vien district, Hoai Nhon prefecture. Several generations later, Nguyen Nhac held the position of a minor clerk (Biện lại) at the Van Don tollgate. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.
