Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. Nguyen Lu was called Duc Ong Bay (Lord Seven) and Nguyen Hue was Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight); Le Trong Ham in the book Minh đô sử argued that Ho Phi Phuc fathered "Nhac, Lu, then two daughters, and then Hue".

Growing up, he, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were sent to study both literature and martial arts with teacher Truong Van Hien. Truong Van Hien was a retainer of Truong Van Hanh, and Truong Van Hanh was the teacher of Nguyen Phuc Luan – Nguyen Anh's father. After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh. It was this teacher who discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel to build a great enterprise. Legend has it that the prophecy "Tay khoi nghia, Bac thu cong" (Rebel in the West, achieve success in the North) originated from Truong Van Hien.[14] Legend also has it that Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were all highly skilled in martial arts and were the founders of several Binh Dinh martial arts styles. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production

The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

Recording
Mike Strange recorded and mixed Eminem's vocals at Effigy Studios in Ferndale, Michigan.[19] The sessions took two days.[20] Strange edited the vocals with D-Verb—a reverberation software—and an Extra Long Delay plug-in. He preferred to make few changes; for "Love the Way You Lie" he almost exclusively used board compression and console equalization. Strange used the Bricasti and Eventide Reverb 2016 mixing tools for "brighter" reverberation. Detroit musician Luis Resto has contributed to the arrangement on many of Eminem's songs, but did not do so for "Love the Way You Lie". According to Strange, "Everything we needed was already in the track, apart from the vocals."[2] Two to three weeks after the sessions, Alex da Kid arrived to help mix and master the track.[11] He wanted to replace the acoustic guitar on the demo, but Eminem chose to keep it.[3] Strange said, "It was simply a matter of trying to match and then to improve on the demo [Alex da Kid]'d sent us."[2] Strange's brother Joe engineered the track.[19]

Rihanna's recording sessions took place at Sun Studios in Dublin, Ireland, and were engineered by Marcos Tovar. The R&B songwriter Makeba Riddick provided additional vocal production.[19] Strange used equalization, compression and reverberation but left the vocal balance. He assumed that Rihanna was satisfied with her recorded vocals and did not make major changes on her seven stereo vocal tracks.[2]

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production

Rihanna's approval of the song's topic ultimately influenced her decision to work with Eminem.
The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Later, local people often called him Duc Ong Binh (Lord Binh)[13] or Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight).[8] According to Quang Trung anh hùng dân tộc (Quang Trung the National Hero), "Nguyen Hue had curly hair, textured skin, eyes that flashed like lightning, a voice as resonant as a bell, agile, strong, and brave." The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. Nguyen Lu was called Duc Ong Bay (Lord Seven) and Nguyen Hue was Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight); Le Trong Ham in the book Minh đô sử argued that Ho Phi Phuc fathered "Nhac, Lu, then two daughters, and then Hue".

Growing up, he, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were sent to study both literature and martial arts with teacher Truong Van Hien. Truong Van Hien was a retainer of Truong Van Hanh, and Truong Van Hanh was the teacher of Nguyen Phuc Luan – Nguyen Anh's father. After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh. It was this teacher who discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel to build a great enterprise. Legend has it that the prophecy "Tay khoi nghia, Bac thu cong" (Rebel in the West, achieve success in the North) originated from Truong Van Hien.[14] Legend also has it that Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were all highly skilled in martial arts and were the founders of several Binh Dinh martial arts styles. question: Describe how the kingdom of Van Lang was organized under the Hung Kings.
answer:
Under the Hung Kings, the kingdom of Van Lang was organized in a structured and centralized manner, reflecting the early political and administrative systems of the Vietnamese people. Here is a detailed description of its organization:

### 1. **Capital and Territory**
- The capital of Van Lang was established in **Phong Chau**, which is located in present-day Bach Hac district. This strategic location helped in governing the kingdom effectively.
- The kingdom bordered the **South Sea to the east**, **Ba Thuc to the west**, **Dong Dinh lake to the north**, and **Ho Ton (Champa, now Quang Nam) to the south**. This geographical positioning allowed for control over key trade routes and natural resources.

### 2. **Administrative Divisions**
- The kingdom was divided into **15 administrative regions**. These regions were:
  - Giao Chi
  - Chu Dien
  - Vu Ninh
  - Phuc Loc
  - Viet Thuong
  - Ninh Hai
  - Duong Tuyen
  - Luc Hai
  - Vu Dinh
  - Hoai Hoan
  - Cuu Chan
  - Binh Van
  - Tan Hung
  - Cuu Duc
- These regions were vassal lands of the **Hung Vuong**, the king, and were under his direct control. This division helped in managing the vast territory efficiently.

### 3. **Government Structure**
- The king, known as **Hung Vuong**, was the supreme ruler of the kingdom. He was supported by a council of officials and military leaders.
- **Civil officials** were called **Lac Hau**, and they were responsible for administrative tasks.
- **Military officials** were called **Lac Tuong**, and they oversaw the defense and military operations of the kingdom.
- The king's **sons** were referred to as **Quan Lang**, and his **daughters** were called **Mi Nuong**. This system ensured a clear line of succession and family involvement in governance.

### 4. **Social and Cultural Practices**
- The people of Van Lang had a strong connection with nature and the environment. They practiced **tattooing** as a means of protection against water monsters, which was a significant cultural and social practice.
- The **tattooing custom** was believed to have originated from the king's advice to the people, who were often harmed by water monsters. By tattooing images of these monsters on their bodies, the people were able to avoid being harmed, thus establishing a tradition that persisted in the region.

### 5. **Legal and Social Order**
- The kingdom was organized with a clear **hierarchical structure**, where the king was at the top, followed by officials, military leaders, and the common people.
- The **feudal system** was in its early stages, with the king assigning his younger sons to govern different regions, thereby establishing a network of loyal vassals.

### 6. **Legacy and Influence**
- The organization of Van Lang under the Hung Kings laid the foundation for the **Vietnamese state** and influenced the development of subsequent dynasties.
- The **Hung Kings** are revered as the **founding ancestors** of the Vietnamese people, and their legacy is celebrated in Vietnamese culture and history.

In summary, the kingdom of Van Lang under the Hung Kings was a well-organized and centralized state with a clear administrative structure, a strong military presence, and a rich cultural heritage that shaped the future of Vietnam.

question: Trace the legendary line from Kinh Duong Vuong to the first Hung Vuong and explain how the Bach Viet people originated.
answer:
The legendary line from **Kinh Duong Vuong** to the **first Hung Vuong** is a foundational narrative in Vietnamese history and mythology, tracing the origins of the **Bach Viet people** (the ancestors of the Vietnamese people). This lineage is deeply rooted in the **Hong Bang Dynasty**, which is believed to have ruled ancient Vietnam before the establishment of the **Van Lang** kingdom.

---

### **1. Kinh Duong Vuong: The First King of the Hong Bang Dynasty**

According to legend, **Kinh Duong Vuong** (also known as **Kinh Duong** or **Kinh Duong Vuong**) was the **first king of the Hong Bang Dynasty**. He is considered the **founder of the Bach Viet people** and the **ancestral ruler of the Vietnamese nation**. His reign marks the beginning of the **mythological era** of Vietnamese history.

- **Kinh Duong Vuong** is said to have ruled for a long time, during which he established the **first centralized rule** over the region that would later become **Vietnam**.
- He is credited with **organizing the people**, **establishing laws**, and **promoting agriculture and culture**.
- His reign is also associated with the **legend of the turtle and the fish**, which symbolizes the **origin of the Vietnamese people** and their connection to the **natural world**.

---

### **2. The Lineage from Kinh Duong Vuong to the First Hung Vuong**

The **lineage from Kinh Duong Vuong to the first Hung Vuong** is a **mythological and historical transition** that marks the **beginning of the Van Lang kingdom** and the **rise of the Hung Kings**.

- **Kinh Duong Vuong** is believed to have **passed the throne to his son**, who later became the **first Hung Vuong** (Hung King).
- The **Hung Kings** (Hung Vuong) were a **line of legendary rulers** who ruled over the **Van Lang kingdom**, which was the **first recorded state** of the Vietnamese people.
- The **first Hung Vuong** is traditionally considered to be **Hung Kings** (Hung Vuong), who were said to be **descendants of Kinh Duong Vuong**.

---

### **3. The Origin of the Bach Viet People**

The **Bach Viet people** (the **Viet people**) are believed to have originated from the **mythological and historical lineage** of **Kinh Duong Vuong** and the **Hung Kings**.

- The **Bach Viet** (meaning "people of the white Viet") are considered the **ancestors of the Vietnamese people**.
- According to legend, the **Bach Viet people** were **descendants of the dragon and the turtle**, which are **symbolic of the Vietnamese people's connection to the land and water**.
- The **legend of the turtle and the fish** is one of the most famous **mythological stories** that explains the **origin of the Bach Viet people**:
  - The **turtle** (symbolizing the **land**) and the **fish** (symbolizing the **water**) were said to have **created the first Vietnamese people**.
  - The **turtle** and the **fish** were also believed to have **given the people their customs, language, and way of life**.

---

### **4. The Role of the Hung Kings in the Formation of the Bach Viet People**

The **Hung Kings** played a **crucial role** in the **formation and development of the Bach Viet people**.

- The **Hung Kings** established the **Van Lang kingdom**, which was the **first state** of the Vietnamese people.
- They **divided the country into 15 administrative regions**, **appointed officials**, and **established a system of governance**.
- They also **introduced customs and traditions**, such as the **tattooing of water monsters** to **protect against water spirits**, which is believed to be the **origin of the tattooing custom** among the **Bach Viet people**.
- The **Hung Kings** are also credited with **promoting agriculture, trade, and cultural development**, which laid the **foundation for the Vietnamese civilization**.

---

### **5. Conclusion**

The **legendary line from Kinh Duong Vuong to the first Hung Vuong** is a **mythological and historical narrative** that explains the **origin of the Bach Viet people** and the **formation of the Vietnamese nation**.

- **Kinh Duong Vuong** is considered the **first king of the Hong Bang Dynasty** and the **founder of the Bach Viet people**.
- The **Hung Kings** were the **successors of Kinh Duong Vuong** and the **founders of the Van Lang kingdom**.
- The **Bach Viet people** are believed to have originated from the **mythological and historical lineage** of these early rulers, and their **culture, customs, and traditions** were shaped by the **legends and practices** of the **Hung Kings**.

This **mythological lineage** is not only a **historical narrative** but also a **symbol of national identity** and **cultural heritage** for the Vietnamese people.

question: Which legends and customs does the document attach to the Hung Vuong era?
answer:
The document attaches the following legends and customs to the **Hung Vuong era**:

### 1. **Tattooing Custom (Ink Tattooing of Water Monsters)**
- **Legend**: The people of Bach Viet (Viet) encountered harm from water monsters (thuong luong) while fishing. The king advised them to tattoo images of water monsters on their bodies using ink. This custom is believed to have originated from this practice.
- **Custom**: The tattooing of images of water monsters became a tradition among the Bach Viet people, likely as a protective measure against these creatures.

### 2. **The Legend of the Child Who Spoke at Three**
- **Legend**: During the reign of the 6th Hung King, a child in Phu Dong village, Vu Ninh region, was born with no speech or laughter. When the country faced an urgent threat, the child suddenly spoke, offering to help the king by granting him a sword and a horse. He then led the army to defeat the enemy and rode into the sky.
- **Custom**: This story is commemorated by the construction of a temple in Phu Dong village, where the child's home garden was renovated for annual sacrifices. The child was later honored as **Xung Thien Than Vuong** (Heavenly General of the Sky).

### 3. **The Legend of Son Tinh and Thuy Tinh (Mountain and Water Spirits)**
- **Legend**: The king had a daughter, Mi Nuong, who was married to Son Tinh (Mountain Spirit). Thuy Tinh (Water Spirit), envious of this union, flooded the land to attack Son Tinh and his wife. Son Tinh used divine powers to defend Tan Vien mountain, and the two spirits eventually became rivals, fighting annually during the high water season.
- **Custom**: This legend is associated with the sacredness of **Tan Vien mountain**, which is considered a high and holy mountain in the Viet country.

### 4. **Feudal System and Administrative Division**
- **Custom**: The Hung Vuong era is described as having a feudal system where the king divided the country into 15 administrative regions. Each region had chiefs and deputies, and the king assigned his younger sons to govern them. This system is considered part of the historical and administrative customs of the time.

### 5. **The Legend of the First Visit to the Zhou Dynasty**
- **Legend**: During the reign of King Cheng of Zhou (1063–1026 BC), the Viet people visited the Zhou dynasty for the first time, claiming to be the Viet Thuong clan and offering a white pheasant. The Duke of Zhou ordered the construction of a **south-pointing chariot** to escort the envoys back to their country.
- **Custom**: This event is seen as an early diplomatic and cultural exchange between the Viet people and the Zhou dynasty, symbolizing the recognition of the Viet kingdom.

These legends and customs reflect the cultural, spiritual, and administrative aspects of the **Hung Vuong era**, highlighting the values, beliefs, and historical significance of this period in Vietnamese history.

question: Summarize Quang Trung's political and military achievements as described in the document.
answer:
Quang Trung, also known as Nguyen Hue, was a prominent leader of the Tay Son rebellion and played a crucial role in the political and military landscape of 18th-century Vietnam. His achievements are summarized as follows:

### **Political Achievements:**
1. **Leadership in the Tay Son Rebellion:**  
   Quang Trung was one of the three brothers (Nguyen Nhac, Nguyen Hue, and Nguyen Lu) who led the Tay Son rebellion against the ruling Le Dynasty and the Trinh lords. He rose to prominence as a key figure in the rebellion, eventually becoming the leader of the Tay Son regime.

2. **Establishment of the Tay Son Dynasty:**  
   After the fall of the Le-Trinh dynasties, Quang Trung helped establish the Tay Son dynasty, which unified Vietnam under a single rule. His leadership was instrumental in consolidating power and ending the centuries-long division between the Le and Trinh factions.

3. **Reform and Governance:**

question: Describe the family background and ancestry of the Tay Son brothers as the document presents it.
answer:
The Tay Son brothers, including Quang Trung (Nguyen Hue), had a complex and evolving family background and ancestry, as presented in the document. According to the historical records, their lineage can be traced back to the Ho family, originally residing in Huong Cai village, Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An province. The Ho family descended from Ho Quy Ly, a historical figure associated with the early Vietnamese dynasties. 

During the reign of Le Than Tong (1653–1657), the Ho family was captured by Lord Nguyen's army and relocated to live in Tuy Vien district, Hoai Nhon prefecture. Over several generations, the family's fortunes changed, and one of their descendants, Nguyen Nhac, held the position of a minor clerk (Biện lại) at the Van Don tollgate. 

Nguyen Nhac's son, Ho Phi Phuc, moved his family to Kien Thanh hamlet. He had three children: the eldest was Nguyen Nhac, the second was Nguyen Hue (Quang Trung), and the third was Nguyen Lu. Ho Phi Phuc's wife was Nguyen Thi Dong, the daughter of a wealthy merchant in Phu Lac. As a result of their marriage, the children of Ho Phi Phuc adopted the mother's surname, Nguyen, changing their surname from Ho to Nguyen. 

Their son, Nguyen Phi Phuc, continued the family's tradition of trade, specializing in the betel trade and achieving prosperity. The document also notes that some sources suggest the Ho family changed their surname to Nguyen as soon as they moved south, aligning with the ruling Nguyen dynasty. 

Thus, the Tay Son brothers' ancestry is rooted in the Ho family, which transitioned to the Nguyen surname through marriage and relocation, ultimately giving rise to the influential Tay Son lineage that would later play a pivotal role in Vietnamese history.

question: How do historians and contemporaries assess Quang Trung's reforms and rule?
answer:
Historians and contemporaries have generally assessed **Quang Trung's (Nguyen Hue)** reforms and rule in highly positive terms, recognizing his leadership, military acumen, and the transformative impact of his policies on Vietnam during the late 18th century. Here is a synthesis of the key assessments:

---

### **1. Military Reforms and Leadership**
- **Military Efficiency and Discipline**: Quang Trung is widely regarded as a brilliant military strategist. His ability to unify the **Tay Son** rebellion and defeat the **Nguyen and Trinh** dynasties demonstrated his tactical genius. His reforms in the military structure, including the establishment of a centralized and disciplined army, were crucial to his success.
- **Use of Technology and Innovation**: He introduced modern military tactics, including the use of **gunpowder weapons**, **cavalry units**, and **military schools**. These innovations helped him outmaneuver and defeat larger, more traditional armies.
- **Symbol of National Unity**: His military campaigns were seen as a unifying force for the Vietnamese people, bringing together different regions and ethnic groups under a common cause.

---

### **2. Administrative and Political Reforms**
- **Centralization of Power**: Quang Trung centralized authority, reducing the power of local lords and nobles. This helped eliminate corruption and inefficiency in governance.
- **Merit-Based Bureaucracy**: He promoted a meritocratic system, encouraging talented individuals to serve the state regardless of their social background. This was a significant departure from the hereditary systems of the past.
- **Legal Reforms**: He introduced legal reforms to ensure justice and fairness, reducing the influence of arbitrary rule and enhancing the rule of law.

---

### **3. Economic Reforms**
- **Agricultural Development**: Quang Trung encouraged agricultural production, particularly in the **Red River Delta**, which was the economic heart of Vietnam. He invested in irrigation systems and land reclamation projects.
- **Trade and Commerce**: He supported trade and commerce, opening up new markets and encouraging the growth of urban centers. His policies helped stimulate economic activity and reduce poverty.
- **Taxation Reforms**: He introduced more equitable taxation systems, reducing the burden on peasants and increasing state revenue.

---

### **4. Cultural and Social Reforms**
- **Promotion of Education**: Quang Trung placed a strong emphasis on education, establishing schools and promoting Confucian values. This helped cultivate a more literate and educated populace.
- **National Identity and Unity**: He fostered a sense of national identity and pride, emphasizing the importance of Vietnamese culture and history. His reign is often seen as a golden age of Vietnamese unity and strength.
- **Religious Tolerance**: Despite being a devout Buddhist, Quang Trung was known for his tolerance of other religions, including Confucianism and Taoism. This helped maintain social harmony and reduce religious tensions.

---

### **5. Contemporaries' Views**
- **Contemporary Accounts**: Contemporary accounts, such as the **"Quang Trung Anh Hùng Dân Tộc"** (National Hero Quang Trung), describe him as a charismatic and visionary leader. His leadership was seen as a beacon of hope for the Vietnamese people during a time of great turmoil.
- **Legacy in Literature and History**: Quang Trung is often portrayed as a national hero in Vietnamese literature and history. His reign is celebrated for its efficiency, fairness, and the prosperity it brought to the country.

---

### **6. Criticisms and Limitations**
- **Short Reign**: One of the most significant criticisms is that Quang Trung's reign was extremely short—only about a year and a half. This limited the full implementation of his reforms.
- **Centralization Concerns**: Some historians argue that his centralization of power may have led to the suppression of local autonomy and potential long-term instability.
- **Military Overreach**: His aggressive military campaigns, while successful, may have left the country vulnerable to future invasions, particularly from the **Chinese Qing dynasty**.

---

### **Conclusion**
Overall, **Quang Trung's reforms and rule are highly praised by historians and contemporaries**. His leadership during a time of great political and social upheaval is seen as a model of efficiency, fairness, and national unity. While his short reign limited the full realization of his vision, his legacy as a national hero and reformer remains deeply embedded in Vietnamese history and culture.

He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. Nguyen Hue was born in the year of Quy Dau 1753, the 13th year of the Canh Hung reign under King Le Hien Tong of the Later Le Dynasty. He was also known as Quang Binh,[11] Van Hue[12], or Ho Thom. Later, local people often called him Duc Ong Binh (Lord Binh)[13] or Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight).[8] According to Quang Trung anh hùng dân tộc (Quang Trung the National Hero), "Nguyen Hue had curly hair, textured skin, eyes that flashed like lightning, a voice as resonant as a bell, agile, strong, and brave." The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. Nguyen Lu was called Duc Ong Bay (Lord Seven) and Nguyen Hue was Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight); Le Trong Ham in the book Minh đô sử argued that Ho Phi Phuc fathered "Nhac, Lu, then two daughters, and then Hue".

Growing up, he, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were sent to study both literature and martial arts with teacher Truong Van Hien. Truong Van Hien was a retainer of Truong Van Hanh, and Truong Van Hanh was the teacher of Nguyen Phuc Luan – Nguyen Anh's father. After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh. It was this teacher who discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel to build a great enterprise. Legend has it that the prophecy "Tay khoi nghia, Bac thu cong" (Rebel in the West, achieve success in the North) originated from Truong Van Hien.[14] Legend also has it that Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were all highly skilled in martial arts and were the founders of several Binh Dinh martial arts styles. Nguyen Hue created Yen Phi Quyen (Swallow Flight Form), Nguyen Lu created Hung Ke Quyen (Rooster Form), and all three Tay Son brothers created Doc Lu Thuong (Single Censer Spear). question: Summarize how critics received "Love the Way You Lie" and the contributions of Eminem and Rihanna.
answer: "Love the Way You Lie" received critical acclaim for its powerful lyrics and emotional depth, which explore themes of love, betrayal, and domestic violence. Critics praised the song for its raw honesty and the way it captures the complexity of a toxic relationship. Eminem and Rihanna's collaboration brought a unique dynamic to the track, with Eminem's verses reflecting his personal struggles and remorse, while Rihanna's vocals conveyed vulnerability and strength. Their combined efforts resulted in a compelling and emotionally resonant piece that resonated with listeners and critics alike.

{"reference_id": "", "content": ""Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery (2010). Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production
Rihanna with red, long hair and a dress with floral patterns. Her left hand is raised and her right-hand holds a microphone near her mouth.
Rihanna's approval of the song's topic ultimately influenced her decision to work with Eminem.
The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

Rihanna's recording sessions took place at Sun Studios in Dublin, Ireland, and were engineered by Marcos Tovar.
